To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

stress and diabetes induce changes in the expression of neurotrophin genes in white adipose tissue (WAT) and brown adipose tissues (BAT), and that these changes are associated with changes in the expression levels of genes coding for proteins involved in the metabolism of carbohydrates, fats, and lipids, and with changes in the levels of proteins involved in insulin signaling.
adipose derived NGF and BDFN are involved in the pathogenesis and treatment of stress and diabetes.
NGF and BDNE are expressed in both WAT and BAT in response to stress and in diabetes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of NGF and BDNF in adipobiology of stress and diabetes.
the adipobiology of NGF and BDNF in stress and diabetes and their possible involvement in the molecular mechanism underlying cardiometabolic diseases.
the adipobiology of NGF and BDGF and its possible involvement in stress and diabetes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
adipose derived neurokines may be considered as potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets in cardiometabolic disorders.
adipose tissue derived NGF and BDFN are important regulators of stress and diabetes, and consequently, they play a role in cardiometabolic diseases.
NGF and/or BDNF are adipokines and that they are involved in the pathogenesis and pathophysiology of stress, diabetes and cardiometabolic disorders.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the adipose derived neurobiologically relevant NGF and BDFN may be involved in stress and diabetes induced metabolic disorders.
the adipose derived NGF and BDFN may be involved in stress and diabetes pathogenesis, and consequently in the development of cardiovascular diseases.
NGF and/or BDNF are stress and/or diabetes induced adipokines that are released from the adipose tissue and may be implicated in stress and diabetes related cardiometabolic disorders.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NGF and, to a lesser extent, BDNF may serve as potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets in stress and diabetes.
the adipose tissues are not only the energy storage depots of the body but they also play a key role in neurobiology, and in stress and metabolic diseases.
NGF and, especially, BDNF may have a role in adipocyte biology, and thus, may be involved in metabolic disorders such as obesity, insulin resistance and diabetes.
